title.value: Environmental Research Letters Effect of irrigation on humid heat extremes OPEN ACCESS RECEIVED

scope_reason: The paper uses paired global climate model simulations to examine how irrigation changes humid heat extremes (wet-bulb temperature) over hot regions.

scope_quote.evidence_text: to estimate the impact of irrigation on humid heat extremes, quantified as different percentiles of wet-bulb temperature (T w ), under contemporary conditions

claims.restatement: Over hot land areas and months, irrigation lowered median daily maximum temperature by ~0.1°C and raised median dew point by ~0.1°C, giving a ~0.03°C rise in median wet-bulb temperature but no significant 90th/99th percentile change.

relation_or_direction.value: slight increase of~0.03 • C ... but no significant change in the 90th or 99th percentiles

geography.value: hot months in land areas overall

support_span.evidence_text: We analyzed global climate model results over hot locations and seasons at high temporal resolution

temporal_frame.value: contemporary conditions (forcings at circa 2000; last 30 of 31 simulated years)

support_span.evidence_text: The No-irrig and Irrigated simulations were each run for 31 years, maintaining the forcings and boundary conditions at the values from circa 2000.
Boundary conditions for our irrigated simulation ('Irrigated') were identical, except for the addition of a seasonal cycle of irrigation forcing, equivalent to rates for year 2000.

evidence.evidence_text: For hot months in land areas overall, irrigation results in a decrease of~0.1 • C in median daily maximum temperature (T 50 , figure 3) and an increase in humidity corresponding to a rise of~0.1 • C in median maximum dew point (T d,50 , figure 3). The cooling and higher humidity combine to yield a slight increase of~0.03 • C in median wet-bulb temperature (T w,50 ), but no significant change in the 90th or 99th percentiles ( figure 3).

claims.restatement: Irrigation slightly increased days with dangerous wet-bulb temperature (≥27°C) over hot areas, from 22.6 to 23.1 days/year (2%), with incidence almost doubling in the Mississippi Valley region (4 to 7 days/year).

evidence.evidence_text: Dangerous conditions with T w ≥ 27 • C slightly increased in frequency overall in hot areas due to irrigation, by a half day per year (going from 22.6 to 23.1 days) or 2% (figure 6). However, changes due to irrigation were pronounced over certain regions, with incidence almost doubling over hot locations in the Mississippi Valley region (from 4 to 7 days per year)
